significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, for many jailbreaks, a distinct safety-verdict-uncertainty state is causally collapsed while harmfulness belief remains high, and that “re-injecting calibrated uncertainty re-triggers the model's cautious/reflective refusal pathway”; this is a form-(ii) causal decomposition augmented by a cross-attack predictive coupling, rather than merely an existence claim. It would establish both a phenomenon—false confidence accompanying jailbreak success—and a mechanism separating uncertainty, harmfulness belief, and refusal action, thereby fixing expectations about which high-harmfulness requests produce compliance and which internal intervention restores refusal; this would materially qualify the refusal-direction account exemplified by Arditi et al., “Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction” (2024). The core branches are determinate: failed separability or causal transfer would rule out this proposed third pathway, while success would support it, although the wording “many jailbreaks” and “an identifiable subset” means a negative result would not decide all jailbreak mechanisms. Topic substitution fails: removing the specific false-confidence decomposition leaves only generic mechanistic LLM safety, which would not justify this above-median score.

reach.justification: The claim hands over two named handles: the measurable “verdict-uncertainty” projection and the “Verdict-Uncertainty Re-injection (VUR)” intervention that “flags abnormally-collapsed verdict uncertainty” conditional on high harmfulness belief. This is ex ante rather than merely post hoc because the activation signal gates an inference-time intervention before the model commits to compliant output, giving deployers an action window. Although directions require per-model calibration, the asserted transferable conclusion is a relation—low verdict uncertainty together with high harmfulness predicts jailbreak compliance, while restoring uncertainty predicts refusal—claimed to be “robust” and “attack-agnostic” across aligned LLMs; after re-extraction, this could guide researchers and practitioners who audit or deploy models, though adaptive joint suppression limits it short of universal reach. Topic substitution again fails: generic safety interpretability supplies neither this runtime signal nor the VUR control knob, so the reach score comes from the claim-specific handle rather than the topic's importance.
